dedupe_keys.name: national grid substation flood defence framework after the 2007 uk floods etr 138

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study describes the flood defence framework for National Grid transmission substations in the United Kingdom. The summer 2007 floods left about half a million people without power and cost more than 3.2 billion pounds, and substation loss cascades into water, transport, communications and health services. Ahead of the Pitt Review the Energy Minister asked for an assessment of substation flood resilience, and an Energy Networks Association task group produced the ETR 138 approach. National Grid first mapped substations exposed to 1 in 100, 200 and 1,000 year floods including climate change under the high UKCP09 scenario, then designed defences: 11 high-risk sites first and 38 medium-risk sites next, aiming at 1 in 1,000 year protection for 2080 or at least 1 in 200 for 2050. The programme began in 2008, cost about 117 million pounds, with 59 million more for surface water from 2021 to 2026, and was approved with BEIS and Ofgem. The page, published in 2019 and updated in 2026, is accessible online as free HTML. Coverage is the United Kingdom. Caveats: flood levels at sites change as modelling improves, and other sectors may work to lower resilience levels. It illustrates substation flood exposure screening and protection standards for resilience and cascading failure studies. Related records: case_study-uk-overhead-line-ratings-rising-temperatures covers another UK network adaptation.
name: National Grid substation flood defence framework after the 2007 UK floods (ETR 138)
outcomes: All 49 critical high and medium risk substations were to be flood-proofed by 2021 at about 117 million GBP, with a further 59 million GBP for surface water risk.
